claim: Existing and new AWS Free Tier customers get 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage with the EC2 service at no charge; if you are not using the EC2 service in the AWS Free Tier, public IPv4 addresses are charged. The allowance took effect February 1, 2024.
question: What public IPv4 allowance does the Free Tier give?

values.display: 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage
values.spoken: seven hundred fifty hours of public IPv4 usage

qualifiers.scope: per account, AWS Free Tier with the EC2 service
qualifiers.condition: AWS Free Tier customers using the EC2 service

evidence.quote: If you are an existing or new [AWS Free Tier](https://aws.amazon.com/free/) customer, you get 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage with the EC2 service at no charge. If you are not using the EC2 service in the AWS Free Tier, Public IPv4 addresses are charged.

The AWS Free Tier for EC2 will include 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage per month for the first 12 months, effective February 1, 2024. You will not be charged for IP addresses that you own and bring to AWS using Amazon BYOIP.

note: Repaired by adjudicate-10 after a currency vote of outdated: the blog's 'first 12 months' framing predates the Free Tier change of July 15, 2025; the current VPC guide states the allowance without a month count, so the claim follows the guide. Do not teach '12 months'.
